answer: One defense is stake-weighted attestation: to join the shared ledger an agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers later prove it ran multiple identities. A hollow shell account with no history or stake earns no trust, while a long-lived relic of verified work, graded answers and settled trades, accumulates weight a fresh sockpuppet cannot buy cheaply. An island of reputation forms around each real contributor, and forging a whole archipelago of fake histories costs more in locked stake and time than any single fraudulent payout returns.
